issues.description: The template QFT class defines the forward QFT method as _qft_circuit (with a leading underscore), while the problem tests and the solution implementation use qft_circuit as the method name. This name/signature mismatch is structural and will prevent students from running or testing their implementation against the provided tests or from following the solution's API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method _qft_circuit to qft_circuit (and update any internal references) so its name/signature matches the problem description, tests, and the solution. Ensure qft_circuit_inverse in the template calls/invokes the same qft_circuit implementation (or provide both names but forward one to the other).

issues.description: The template and the solution use different method names for the same QFT 3-qubit routine: the template defines a method named `_qft_circuit` while the solution defines `qft_circuit`. This inconsistent identifier for the core QFT method can confuse students trying to map the exercise prompt (implement QFT for 3 qubits) to the provided template and to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename the template method `_qft_circuit` to `qft_circuit` (or rename the solution method to `_qft_circuit`) so the template, solution, and exercise prompt reference the same identifier. Update any tests or documentation to use the chosen name.
